newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Oct M2 supply rises 18.9 pct on year. [CORRECTED 04:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Oct M2 supply rises 18.9 pct on year. [CORRECTED 04:25 GMT]

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose year-on-year 18.9 percent in October (Corrects from February), against a 13.9 percent rise a year earlier, provisional Bank of Korea (BOK) figures showed on Thursday. (All figures in percent)
Note - M2 consists of money in circulation, checking account and savings account deposits with banks.
The BOK said in a statement the October M2 rise was higher than a year ago because of a deposit shift from trust accounts to savings accounts in banks.
Money in trust accounts had fallen steadily since May, when the maturity of the accounts was extended by up to six months, a BOK official said.
He said tax breaks given to household depositors at savings accounts, effective from October, also prompted the shift.
Private sector credit grew by 3.47 trillion won in the month, compared with a rise of 4.28 trillion won a year ago.
In October, the state's budget revenue was 2.82 trillion won more than budget spending. A year ago, budget revenue was 1.98 trillion won higher than spending.
Capital outflows were 890 billion won larger than inflows from overseas in October. A year earlier inflows were 360 billion won more, the bank statement said.
Net issues of certificates for deposits totalled 1.2 trillion won in October. A year ago, CD repayments were 269 billion won more than issues.
